issues.description: The problem text lists the lecture attributes in one order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) but the UML diagram later presents them in a different order (numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors). The instructions explicitly ask students to follow the UML order when creating the constructor, so this contradiction in the problem statement can confuse students about the required constructor parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute order consistent: either update the textual list or the UML so both present the same attribute sequence. Also clarify in the instructions which exact constructor parameter order students should implement (preferably include an explicit constructor signature in the template or problem statement).

issues.description: The solution's constructor parameter order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) does not match the attribute order shown in the UML diagram in the problem statement (which lists numberOfInscribedStudents first). Because the task requires students to follow the UML order for the constructor parameters, this mismatch between the solution and the UML can lead to confusion and failing tests if the tests expect the UML order.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution constructor parameter order with the UML (or update the UML/text to match the solution). Additionally, provide an explicit constructor signature in the template or problem statement so students and reference solutions use the same parameter ordering.
